phys-em-01-c1.text: OpenStax (Samuel J. Ling, Jeff Sanny, William Moebs) (2016). University Physics Volume 2, 5.1 Electric Charge. OpenStax, Rice University.
phys-em-01-c1.quote: the charge on any object—the charge on all objects—must be an integer multiple of this amount
phys-em-01-c1.claim: Charge is also quantised, so all charges are multiples of the elementary charge e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, the charge of a proton.

phys-em-02-c2.text: J J O'Connor and E F Robertson. Michael Faraday (1791 - 1867) - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics.
phys-em-02-c2.quote: He showed that a magnet could induce an electrical current in a wire.
phys-em-02-c2.claim: Michael Faraday's 1831 discovery: a changing magnetic flux through a loop induces an electromotive force (voltage) in the loop.

phys-em-02-c3.quote: The ampere is that constant current which, if maintained in two straight parallel conductors of infinite length, of negligible circular cross-section, and placed 1 meter apart in vacuum, would produce between these conductors a force equal to 2 x 10 -7 newton per meter of length.
phys-em-02-c3.claim: This is how the ampere (unit of current) was historically defined: by the force between parallel wires.

phys-em-03-c2.text: J J O'Connor and E F Robertson. James Clerk Maxwell - Biography. MacTutor History of Mathematics.
phys-em-03-c2.quote: He proposed that the phenomenon of light is therefore an electromagnetic phenomenon.
phys-em-03-c2.claim: Maxwell concluded light is an electromagnetic wave.

phys-em-04-c2.text: Thomas Young's Double Slit Experiment. Molecular Expressions Microscopy Primer, Florida State University.
phys-em-04-c2.quote: In 1801, an English physicist named Thomas Young performed an experiment that strongly inferred the wave-like nature of light.
phys-em-04-c2.claim: Young's double-slit experiment (1801) showed light interferes, alternating bright and dark bands.

phys-em-04-c1.text: NASA. Introduction to the Electromagnetic Spectrum. NASA Science.
phys-em-04-c1.quote: The human eye can only detect only a small portion of this spectrum called visible light.
phys-em-04-c1.claim: Visible light (400–700 nm) is a tiny sliver.

phys-em-05-c1.text: Nobel Prize Outreach (1965). The Nobel Prize in Physics 1965. NobelPrize.org.
phys-em-05-c1.quote: The Nobel Prize in Physics 1965 was awarded jointly to Sin-Itiro Tomonaga, Julian Schwinger and Richard P. Feynman "for their fundamental work in quantum electrodynamics, with deep-ploughing consequences for the physics of elementary particles"
phys-em-05-c1.claim: QED, developed by Feynman, Schwinger, and Tomonaga (Nobel 1965), describes how charged particles interact by exchanging virtual photons.

phys-em-06-c2.text: R Nave. Lenz's Law. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-em-06-c2.quote: the polarity of the induced emf is such that it produces a current whose magnetic field opposes the change which produces it.
phys-em-06-c2.claim: The minus sign (Lenz's law) means induced currents oppose the change that produced them.

phys-em-07-c1.text: R Nave. Dielectric Constant. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-em-07-c1.quote: The factor k by which the effective field is decreased by the polarization of the dielectric is called the dielectric constant of the material.
phys-em-07-c1.claim: The result: the field inside is reduced by a factor of the dielectric constant κ.

phys-em-07-c2.text: R Nave. Ferromagnetism. HyperPhysics, Georgia State University.
phys-em-07-c2.quote: Iron, nickel, cobalt and some of the rare earths (gadolinium, dysprosium) exhibit a unique magnetic behavior which is called ferromagnetism
phys-em-07-c2.claim: Ferromagnetic materials (iron, nickel, cobalt) align with it strongly and retain magnetization after the field is removed.

phys-em-08-c1.text: (2021). Synchrotron light sources and X-ray free-electron-lasers. arXiv.
phys-em-08-c1.quote: synchrotron light sources consist of electron circular accelerators and produce synchrotron radiation in bending magnets and undulators.
phys-em-08-c1.claim: This is why radio antennas are oscillators (charges accelerating back and forth) and why electron synchrotrons emit x-rays (charges in circular motion).
